home.title: Olauda: homework and timetable changes for your whole class
home.description: Homework, exams and timetable changes in one place your whole class shares. One person adds it, everyone sees it. Free and without ads.

features.title: Features — Olauda
features.description: Tasks, timetable, schedule changes, groups, announcements and private tasks: everything Olauda does, and the limits that come with it.

about.title: About — Olauda
about.description: Why Olauda exists, what we won't do with it, and who runs it.

contact.title: Contact — Olauda

hero.title: Your class, always on the same page.
hero.lede: Olauda keeps homework, exams and timetable changes in one place your whole class shares. One person adds it, everyone sees it. Free, without ads.
hero.invite_hint: Got an invite link from your class? Open it and you're in.

day.label: Sample timetable
day.caption: A sample week that runs on your clock. During school hours, the blue line shows where your day would be right now.

everyone.title: Entered once. There for everyone.
everyone.body: Whoever hears about it first adds it: Thursday's homework, the maths lesson that's off, the room change. Everyone else sees it straight away, without asking around.

tasks.title: Homework and exams
tasks.body: With due date, description and attachments. Photos, PDFs, Word, PowerPoint and Excel files can all be attached.

changes.title: Timetable changes
changes.body: Cancellations, substitutions and room changes show up right in the timetable, for the people they affect.

announcements.title: Announcements
announcements.body: Short notices for the whole group. The important ones are marked so they stand out.

roles.title: Who can change what
roles.body: Owners, admins, moderators and members. You decide which role may add tasks, enter changes or post.

roster.label: Example: one change reaching a class of 28

you.title: Shared list, personal checkmarks.
you.body: Ticking off homework, pinning what matters and archiving what's done only changes your own view. Nobody sees what you've finished, and you can't mess up anyone else's list.

checks.title: Ticked off, pinned, archived
checks.body: Your progress, kept to yourself. Finished tasks move out of the way when you want them to.

courses.title: Only your courses
courses.body: In Abitur year groups everyone picks their courses once. Lessons and tasks from the others stay hidden.

private.title: Private tasks
private.body: A to-do list only you can see, stored encrypted. Not even your group's admins can read it.

specimen.label: Example task list
specimen.hidden: {count} task from other courses hidden | {count} tasks from other courses hidden

create.title: Create a group
create.body: Pick a standard group for a class that has every lesson together, or an Abitur group for the course system.

timetable.title: Enter the timetable
timetable.body: Periods, breaks and lessons, once for everyone. Each day can have its own break plan.

invite.title: Invite your class
invite.body: Share the invite link or let people scan the QR code. You can revoke links at any time.

courses.title: Everyone picks their courses
courses.body: Each member chooses their own once. From then on, they only see what concerns them.

items.a: No. There's no subscription, no premium tier and no advertising. Everyone gets the whole thing.

items.q: Does our school or our teachers need to take part?
items.a: No. Anyone can create a group for their class or year group and invite the others. The school doesn't need to set anything up.

items.q: Who can see what I enter?
items.a: Tasks, the timetable and announcements are visible to members of the group. Your checkmarks, pins and private tasks are visible only to you.
On servers in Germany. Attachments and emails go through a few service providers, all of which are listed in the privacy policy. Private tasks are stored encrypted with AES-256.

items.q: How do I keep my account safe?
items.a: Sign in with a password, Google or a passkey, and turn on two-factor authentication with any authenticator app. You can see every device you're signed in on and sign them out.

items.q: I'm under 18. Can I use Olauda?
items.a: Yes, as long as a parent or guardian agrees. You confirm that when you sign up.

items.q: Can I take my data with me, or delete it?
items.a: Both, whenever you like. Your account settings export everything as a ZIP file, and you can delete your account there yourself.

closing.title: Bring your class along.
closing.body: Create an account, set up a group and send your class the link. That's all it takes.

features.title: Everything Olauda does
features.lede: A complete list, including the limits. If something's missing here, Olauda doesn't do it yet.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.body: Homework, exams and Dalton assignments for the whole group live in one list. Someone adds a task once, and everyone has it. If the same task already exists, you're asked before a duplicate appears.
items: Homework, exams and, if your group uses it, Dalton
Title, subject, course, due date and a description with formatting
Photos up to 2 MB, PDF, Word, PowerPoint and Excel files up to 5 MB
One shared note per task, for whoever is allowed to write it
By type and subject, with completed and archived tasks hidden if you like
Tick off, pin and archive without changing anyone else's list

timetable.title: Timetable
timetable.body: The timetable is set up once for the group and looks the same for everyone, except that each member sees only their own courses. Changes are entered for a single week and show up straight away.
items: The whole week on large screens, one day at a time on phones
Cancellations, substitutions, room changes and moved lessons
The running or next lesson stands out, and on phones a marker shows the current time
Shown with their length, with breaks counted in if you prefer
Lessons, rooms and lengths, with undo and redo
Start time, lesson length and breaks, separately for every weekday

groups.title: Groups and roles
groups.body: A group is a class, a year group or a club. Whoever creates it owns it and decides what everyone else may do.
items: Standard groups for classes, Abitur groups with basic, advanced and additional courses
Links and QR codes that expire after seven days and can be revoked
Thirteen of them, each set to the lowest role that may use it
Remove people, or ban them if they shouldn't come back

announcements.title: Announcements
announcements.body: A school trip, an early finish, a moved exam: announcements appear at the top of the app for every member until they've read them.
items: Up to 160 characters, so they stay readable at a glance
Marked in red when it matters
Shown one after another, all dismissable in one go

private.title: Private tasks
private.body: A to-do list that belongs to you alone: the present to buy, the book to finish. Nobody else can see it, not even your group's admins.
items: Drag to reorder, duplicate and tick off

search.title: Search and shortcuts
search.body: Press Ctrl K, or ⌘ K on a Mac, anywhere in the app. Type a few letters to jump to a page or start an action.
items: Pages, settings and actions in one list
Alt N, or Alt P for a private one

account.title: Account and security
account.body: Your account is protected by a confirmed email address, optional two-factor authentication and an overview of every device you're signed in on.
items: Any authenticator app, with recovery codes as a backup
See where you're signed in and sign out remotely
Export everything as a ZIP file at any time
Delete your account yourself, without asking anyone
Light, dark or system theme, German or English

about.title: Why Olauda exists
about.lede: Homework used to get lost in long message threads. You found out about a canceled lesson at the classroom door. Olauda is the one place where all of it gets written down once.

story.title: Built one real need at a time
story.body: It started with a shared homework list. Invite links, roles, a timetable editor, courses for Abitur year groups and Dalton support followed, each because a class actually needed it. Nothing was added to fill a feature list.

principles.title: What we won't do
items: No subscriptions, no premium tier. Everyone gets the whole product.
There's no advertising, and there won't be.
We collect what the service needs to run and nothing else. Private tasks are encrypted, passwords are only stored as a hash.
Every feature has to solve a real problem at school. Whatever doesn't gets cut.

team.title: Who runs it
team.body: Olauda is an independent project, built and run by a small team in its spare time. There's no company and no investor behind it. Want to help, or have an idea? We'd like to hear it.

contact.title: Get in touch
contact.lede: Questions, bugs, ideas for new features: we read everything and reply as soon as we can.

discord.title: Discord
discord.body: Talk to other people using Olauda, share ideas and reach us directly.

status.title: System status
status.body: Check whether something is down before you write to us.

bugs.title: Found a bug?
bugs.body: Tell us what you did, what you expected and what happened instead. A screenshot helps.

not_found.title: Free period.
not_found.body: This page doesn't exist. Maybe it was moved, or the link has a typo.

cookie.text: We only use cookies the site needs to work. We count visits with Umami, without cookies or profiles.

footer.tagline: Homework and timetable changes, shared with your class.
